summary: David Graeber studied at Phillips Academy, SUNY Purchase, and the University of Chicago under Marshall Sahlins (~1987–1998). He later held posts at Yale University (1998–2007), Goldsmiths (2007–2013), and the London School of Economics (~2013–2020).

David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He was affiliated with the University of Vienna as Dr. (attested 2015) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies as a Research Fellow (attested 2026).

David J. Kalupahana specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at the University of Ceylon and SOAS University of London. He served at the University of Ceylon (~1959–1972) and became Chairman of the Philosophy Department at the University of Hawaiʻi in 1972.

David Jones, a scholar of philosophy and religious studies, earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. By 2007, he served as a philosophy professor at the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

Historian David K. Wyatt studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell. He taught at SOAS (~1962–1968) and the University of Michigan (~1968–1969), chaired the Cornell University Department of History (1969–2002), and served as president of the Association for Asian Studies (1993).

David Kerman Tomlinson specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold (attested 2019), also studying under Jay L. Garfield and Andrew Rotman, and held a post at Smith College.
David Kopf was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Chicago (~1957–1964) and held a post at the University of Minnesota from ~1967 to 2003.

David L. Gosling works in the fields of religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, University of Cambridge in 1992, and was affiliated with the University of Cambridge in 2001.

David L. Haberman is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1972–1976). He held posts at the University of Arizona (~1989–1993) and Indiana University Bloomington (~1993–2021; Emeritus ~2021).

David L. McMahan specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and the University of Vermont, before holding assistant (attested 2002) and full professor (attested 2013) posts at Franklin & Marshall College.

David Ludden is a historian and Indologist who studied at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at Virginia (1979–1980), Penn (1981–2008), BRAC University (2005), and New York University (from 2007).

David M. DiValerio works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at SIT Graduate Institute and the University of Virginia (PhD under Kurtis R. Schaeffer) and held a post at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2015).

David M. Knipe is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who held a long career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as professor (attested 1975–2001), chair of religious studies (attested 1989), and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

David Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, including as director (attested 2004, 2013), and is attested as President Emeritus at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 2026.

David N. Lorenzen studied at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University (doctorate under A. L. Basham). He worked primarily at El Colegio de México (1970–2010; emeritus 2019) in Asian and African studies, alongside several visiting professorships.

David Ownby studied at Vanderbilt and Harvard (Ph.D.). A historian of China and religion, he taught at Southern Methodist University (~1989–1993) and served as Professor of History at the University of Montreal (1994–2023).

David P. Jackson studied Tibetology and Buddhist studies at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg and Dezhung Rinpoche. He held a C-3 professorship at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007) along with posts in Austria.

David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa (attested 1993), also studying with Geshe Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

David Pingree studied at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer. In history and Indology, he held posts at Harvard, Chicago (1963–1971), Brown University (from 1971), and Cornell (1981–1986, 1995).

David Quinter is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Colorado and Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later serving as associate professor of East Asian religions at the University of Alberta (attested 2019).
